prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant: intake–header; distribution monitored. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station; Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid; Cobalt=North Filter Gallery; Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench; Lantern=SCADA Historian Server; Quarry=Maintenance Planner; Juniper=High Service Pump Header; Falcon=Distribution Dispatcher. Items: Raw Water Screen Channel→Quarry:Rake Torque Snapshot; Marigold→Laboratory Technician:Alum Batch Ticket; technician produces Sample Chain Slip; Sparrow receives samples/produces checked Jar Test Photograph Set (“the set”:dose confirmation); South Filter Gallery→Chief Operator:Filter Run Exception Note; Chemical Supplier Driver:Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; Clearwell Level Controller:Clearwell Diver Entry Permit after level/isolation verification; Juniper:threshold-triggered Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; Chief Operator:Backwash Solids Manifest after quantity/handling verification; Residuals Hauler removes residuals. Requirements: intake permissives; losses alarm/stop. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode:intensified monitoring/constrained production. Dosing within approved limits/review; unreliable indications hold last-approved dose. Samples require custody/acceptance/analysis; late/warm troubleshooting-only; field results provisional. Backwash Recovery Tank receives washwater; return requires settling/verified clarity; poor quality isolate/settle-decant. Cobalt staggers verified washes; South Filter Gallery breakthrough/delayed ripening excludes until approval. Maintenance/overrides require approval/isolation/monitoring/evidence/restoration; failed tests remain open. Lantern retains synchronized reconstruction data. Chief Operator classifies upsets by quality risk/capacity/alarm persistence/service impact: advisory=monitor/document; controlled=operator changes loading/filter-to-waste/sampling/recovery hold; critical=immediate quality protection, notify Duty Engineer if automation inadequate. Chlorine Residual Alarm during filtration upset protects finished water; pauses maintenance/holds increases. Jointly monitor Chlorine Contact Basin/Clearwell Level Controller for contact/storage/demand. Juniper maintains stable delivery; pressure/flow/status indicate demand. Notify Falcon of North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station reserve impacts; compare sustained pressure/reservoir/pump/field trends before setpoints. North:separate suction/discharge/availability/communications; South:lead-booster starts after sustained below-band delay. Repeated solids problems notify Quarry. Resume normal:stable recovery quality,residuals

New part:
S181: When a distribution station is in automatic operation, local controls are expected to sequence pumps within approved limits and report abnormal starts, failures, or valve positions to the control system.
S182: When a distribution station is in local or manual operation, the Distribution Dispatcher records the reason, the expected duration, and the field contact responsible for the change.
S183: The Clearwell Level Controller is checked before large distribution adjustments so that high service pumping does not create avoidable level instability.
S184: The Chief Operator may direct a conservative pumping posture during unusual demand, main repair activity, or recovery from a treatment upset.
S185: The Duty Engineer reviews persistent low-pressure complaints, repeated station alarms, or mismatches between observed pressure and modeled expectations.
S186: Cobalt shall provide a reliable filter service status indication before the control room treats increased distribution demand as available finished-water capacity.
S187: Sparrow records incoming distribution check samples with the pressure zone, collection point, and time needed for control-room review.
S188: The SCADA Historian Server uses the Sample Chain Slip to associate distribution water-quality entries with the operating period shown in the electronic log.
S189: The Distribution Dispatcher sends the Pressure Zone Handoff Card after verifying current pressure-zone setpoints, active alarms, and open field work.
S190: Shift handoff includes any disabled alarms, temporary operating limits, pending station inspections, and customer complaint trends that may affect dispatch decisions.
S191: If communication to a distribution station is lost, the control room assumes the last confirmed operating mode remains in effect until field verification or telemetry restoration proves otherwise.
S192: Field crews notify the control room before opening or closing major distribution valves so that pressure changes can be distinguished from pump or instrumentation problems.
S193: The Distribution Dispatcher coordinates planned hydrant flushing, valve exercising, and main isolation work with pumping schedules to limit avoidable pressure swings.
S194: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, distribution pressure decisions remain coordinated with water-quality response actions rather than being treated as a purely hydraulic issue.
S195: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench provides analytical status through normal plant reporting channels, and the control room uses that status to interpret pressure-zone complaints involving taste, odor, or disinfectant concerns.
S196: The SCADA Historian Server retains pressure, flow, pump status, and alarm data needed to reconstruct dispatch decisions after an event.
S197: During Storm Intake Mode, the Distribution Dispatcher avoids unnecessary zone changes unless demand, storage, or public-safety conditions require action.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
